div.div: GPU load alone costs the depth camera service no frames; shared-pool CPU wait costs it frames (0.3 Hz at half the full stack's wait [camera_pool_loss_hz: half_full_wait, illustrative]; the higher arm is void), so the pool verdict is "undecided at dose"

Factor 3: the full stack's extra topic subscribers (fan-out) cost 1 Hz [camera_fanout_loss_hz, illustrative]. Each factor's part of the full stack's 5 Hz camera loss:
loss, Hz
fan-out 1 Hz, share 0.2
rest 4 Hz: not attributed (pool share undecided; loads not tested together)

GPU part 0 Hz (no segment). Shares are my estimate from `camera_fanout_loss_hz`, `camera_full_stack_loss_hz` and `camera_gpu_only_loss_hz`; a post-hoc reading that keeps the VOID arm gives the pool a larger part and does not replace the verdict.

Setup. The depth camera service keeps 30 Hz alone [camera_hz_alone, illustrative]. One factor per window, idle pool unless the factor is the pool. In the full stack it falls to 25 Hz (my estimate from `camera_hz_alone` and `camera_full_stack_loss_hz`).

Pre-registered verdicts
• GPU: minor. No loss at any GPU dose tested.
• Shared pool: "undecided at dose". The valid arm is below the full stack's wait.
• Fan-out: a minor share, about one fifth of the full-stack loss.

Caveats. The three loads were not tested together. The GPU arms ran with frame-time slack that the full stack does not leave, and the full stack + VLA dose lies beyond the highest GPU arm. The two panels use different x axes; the black square is the same full-stack reference on the pool axis. The dotted line joins all pool arms, the VOID one included (post-hoc reading). Values are an illustrative measurement.

Correction kept visible. The camera's loss is CPU-side; GPU load alone costs it nothing. Read with page 06: the detector's GPU wait follows the others' GPU share, the camera's frame rate does not. Same GPU, different victims: the dose curve is per service, not per board (interpretation).

Legend
green line + circles = GPU arms (valid), no dose values given
filled blue circle = valid pool arm; hollow dashed blue circle = VOID window
hollow solid blue circle = alone (zero loss by definition)
black square = full-stack reference (all loads)
grey dashed line = full-stack loss level
grey shading = pool waits above the full stack's
dotted = post-hoc reading; light-blue hatch = fan-out (CPU-side)

Sources. Note B1, "The camera is different". Pool-arm x positions come from the field names of camera_pool_loss_hz (half / twice the full stack's wait). How to benchmark a robot stack: ../../robot-workload-benchmarking/.
Illustrative (round teaching numbers that keep the shape of a finding; not measurements): camera_pool_loss_hz, camera_full_stack_loss_hz, camera_gpu_only_loss_hz, camera_fanout_loss_hz, camera_hz_alone.
